Definition: {a large public building, such as a palace or temple}
BiblicalUsage: hêykal — palace, temple. That is the whole of it, and it is enough: 10 occurrences, and in Ezra and Daniel the meaning never wavers. I keep coming back to the simple reading because the simple reading is the true one.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hêykal matters because God put His name in the temple so His people would know where to find Him. I hold that the simple reading is the true one, and I will not trade it for a clever one.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
